title: Customer health vitals KPI worksheet
summary: Working worksheet for QBR-facing CS teams to compute, standardize and report four core inference KPIs: latency, uptime, cost per token, and cache hit rate. Includes measurement rules, common data-source mappings, tiered targets, and a compact tracker table for export into QBR decks.
metric_definitions: Latency (per-route): measured as server-side request-to-first-byte and end-to-end token generation; report p50/p95/p99. Uptime: percent of accepted requests that returned a 2xx response within the SLA window, measured per region and per model route. Cost/token: billable cost divided by billed tokens for the reporting period; normalize to cents per 1k tokens. Cache hit rate: fraction of requests that reused a cached prefix/KV entry resulting in >=1 token generation avoided; report both prefix-hit % and KV-cache % where available.
measurement_guidelines: Data sources: use Redwood Console routing logs for latency and cache probes, billing export for cost/token, and healthcheck/uptime SLI in SRE metrics for uptime. Calculation rules: - Latency p95/p99 should be computed on successful 2xx responses only; exclude synthetic probes. - Uptime denominator = total accepted requests during period; numerator = requests that completed within SLA latency threshold and returned 2xx. - Cost/token should exclude refunds, internal test volume, and apply credits before dividing by billable tokens. - Cache hit rate: only count requests routed to cache-enabled model variants. Edge cases: warmup/burst periods can skew p99; flag windows that include deploys/manual load tests.

alert_playbook: When a KPI breaches threshold: 1) Triage: confirm data source (Console vs billing export) and time window. 2) Scope: is it specific to a customer route, region, or model variant? 3) Short-term mitigation: route to lower-latency variant, enable burst capacity, or rollback recent model change. 4) Long-term action: open APM/SRE incident with tags, schedule tuning (batching/quantization), add to next optimization sprint. Example runbook links included in linked_artifacts. Escalation matrix: CS -> Solutions Eng -> Infra -> SRE -> Product for cross-functional changes.
common_pitfalls_and_notes: - Mixing client-side and server-side latency will inflate numbers; always prefer server-side telemetry for SLAs. - Billing lag: cost/token computed from billing export may lag usage by 48–72 hours; call out period alignment in QBR slides. - Synthetic test traffic should be filtered out of cost and latency calculations. - Cache hit behavior is workload-dependent; report workload characteristics (avg prompt length, reuse patterns) alongside hit rate. - For enterprise customers with Dedicated, include a separate Dedicated-capacity row because cost math and SLAs differ.
examples: Example calculation (Latency p95): Query set = production 2xx requests from 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28; p95 = 172 ms. Example Cost/token: Charges = $3,240; billable tokens = 9,600,000 => cost per 1k tokens = (3240)/(9600) = $0.3375 per 1k tokens. Example Cache hit: prefix_hits=18,000, cache_eligible=45,000 => 40% prefix hit rate.
